```{r}
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project) != project) project <- dirname(project)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")))
x <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/audit_times.csv"))$audit_days
restaurants <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/restaurant_ratings.csv"))
quality_levels <- c("Good", "Very Good", "Excellent")
restaurants$quality_rating <- factor(restaurants$quality_rating, levels = quality_levels, ordered = TRUE)
q6 <- function(v, p) unname(quantile(v, p, type = 6))
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
box_record <- function(v, g) {
  q <- q6(v, c(.25,.5,.75)); iqr <- q[3]-q[1]
  lo <- q[1]-1.5*iqr; hi <- q[3]+1.5*iqr
  inside <- v[v >= lo & v <= hi]
  data.frame(Group=g, ymin=min(inside), Q1=q[1], Median=q[2], Q3=q[3], ymax=max(inside), Lo=lo, Hi=hi)
}
```

## 1. Center

```{r}
counts <- table(x)
modes <- as.numeric(names(counts)[counts == max(counts)])
kable(data.frame(Measure = c("n", "Sum (days)", "Mean (days)", "Median (days)", "Mode (days)"),
                 Value = c(length(x), sum(x), mean(x), median(x), modes)), digits = 2)
stopifnot(length(x)==20, sum(x)==385, mean(x)==19.25, median(x)==18,
          identical(modes,18), sort(x)[10]==18, sort(x)[11]==18)
```

Positions **10 and 11** determine the median. Both contain 18 days. The mode is **18**, occurring three times; R's `mode()` reports storage mode rather than a frequency maximum.

The average duration of these 20 audits is **19.25 days**, while their middle duration is **18 days**. Longer observations increase the mean relative to the median. Neither establishes a future deadline because the data are a sample of historical audits and future scope, staffing, and conditions may differ.

## 2. Variability and units

```{r}
ss <- sum((x-mean(x))^2)
kable(data.frame(Measure = c("Minimum (days)", "Maximum (days)", "Range (days)",
                            "Squared deviations (days squared)", "Sample variance (days squared)", "Sample SD (days)",
                            "Variance with denominator n (days squared)"),
                 Value = c(min(x),max(x),diff(range(x)),ss,ss/(length(x)-1),sqrt(ss/(length(x)-1)),ss/length(x))), digits=4)
stopifnot(abs(ss/(length(x)-1)-var(x))<1e-10, abs(sqrt(ss/(length(x)-1))-sd(x))<1e-10,
          diff(range(x))==21)
```

The sample variance is approximately **29.5658 days²**; sample SD is **5.4374 days**. With denominator `n`, variance is **28.0875 days²**, describing these observations with that population-style denominator. The relevant population is defined by the question, not the file boundary. The usual unbiased sample-variance claim requires independent sampling from a common population with finite variance.

## 3. Quartiles, fences, and whiskers

```{r}
q <- q6(x,c(.25,.5,.75)); iqr <- q[3]-q[1]
audit_box <- box_record(x,"Audit")
flagged <- x[x < audit_box$Lo | x > audit_box$Hi]
kable(data.frame(Quantity=c("Minimum","Q1","Median","Q3","Maximum","IQR","Lower fence","Upper fence","Lower whisker","Upper whisker"),
                 Days=c(min(x),q,max(x),iqr,audit_box$Lo,audit_box$Hi,audit_box$ymin,audit_box$ymax)))
stopifnot(identical(q,c(15,18,22)),iqr==7,audit_box$Lo==4.5,audit_box$Hi==32.5,
          audit_box$ymin==12,audit_box$ymax==28,identical(as.integer(flagged),33L))
ggplot(audit_box,aes(Group,ymin=ymin,lower=Q1,middle=Median,upper=Q3,ymax=ymax)) +
  geom_boxplot(stat="identity",width=.35,fill="#B6D2E2") +
  geom_point(data=data.frame(Group="Audit",Days=flagged),aes(Group,Days),inherit.aes=FALSE,colour="#B47816",size=3) +
  labs(x=NULL,y="Audit duration (days)",title="Type-6 quartiles and 1.5-IQR fences")
```

The overall maximum is **33**, retained in the five-number summary. It lies above the **32.5** fence, so the upper whisker stops at the largest observed value inside the fences: **28**. Check the source record and audit circumstances. A flag alone does not establish an error or justify removing valid data.

## 4. Hypothetical sensitivity and relative measures

```{r}
y <- x; y[which.max(y)] <- 60
summary_values <- function(v) c(Mean=mean(v),Median=median(v),SD=sd(v),Range=diff(range(v)),IQR=diff(q6(v,c(.25,.75))))
kable(rbind(Original=summary_values(x),Hypothetical=summary_values(y)),digits=2)
cv <- 100*sd(x)/mean(x); z <- (33-mean(x))/sd(x)
kable(data.frame(Measure=c("Original CV (%)","Original 33-day z-score"),Value=c(cv,z)),digits=3)
stopifnot(max(x)==33,mean(y)==20.6,median(y)==18,diff(range(y))==48,
          diff(q6(y,c(.25,.75)))==7,abs(cv-28.2464589)<1e-5,abs(z-2.5287624)<1e-5)
```

Mean increases from **19.25 to 20.60**, sample SD from **5.44 to 10.25**, and range from **21 to 48 days**. Median remains **18** and IQR **7** for this particular change. This demonstrates different sensitivities; it does not establish that median/IQR are always preferable.

The original CV is **28.25%**: sample SD is about 28.25% of the sample mean. Elapsed duration has a meaningful zero and positive mean. Celsius has an arbitrary zero, so changing its scale changes the relative variability calculation without changing the underlying temperatures.

The original 33-day z-score is approximately **2.53**. The IQR and z-score rules use different summaries and cutoffs and may flag different observations. A z-score is not automatically a probability or a declaration of normality.

## 5. Restaurant comparisons

```{r}
groups <- split(restaurants$meal_price_usd,restaurants$quality_rating)
tab <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(groups),function(g){
 v<-groups[[g]];q<-q6(v,c(.25,.75))
 data.frame(Quality=g,N=length(v),Mean=mean(v),Median=median(v),SD=sd(v),Q1=q[1],Q3=q[2],IQR=diff(q))
}))
kable(tab,digits=2)
stopifnot(identical(tab$N,c(84L,150L,66L)),identical(tab$Median,c(19.5,25,34.5)),
          identical(tab$IQR,c(10,12,11.5)),diff(tab$Median[c(1,3)])==15)
boxes <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(groups),function(g)box_record(groups[[g]],g)))
boxes$Group <- factor(boxes$Group,levels=quality_levels,ordered=TRUE)
points <- do.call(rbind,lapply(names(groups),function(g){
 r<-box_record(groups[[g]],g);v<-groups[[g]];o<-v[v<r$Lo|v>r$Hi]
 data.frame(Group=rep(g,length(o)),Price=o)
}))
points$Group<-factor(points$Group,levels=quality_levels,ordered=TRUE)
ggplot(boxes,aes(Group,ymin=ymin,lower=Q1,middle=Median,upper=Q3,ymax=ymax))+
 geom_boxplot(stat="identity",width=.5,fill="#B6D2E2")+
 geom_point(data=points,aes(Group,Price),inherit.aes=FALSE,colour="#B47816",size=2.5)+
 labs(x="Quality rating",y="Meal price (USD)",title="Group comparisons with consistent quartiles")
```

Excellent has the highest median (**USD 34.50**), compared with **USD 19.50** for Good: a **USD 15 difference between group medians**. Good has the smallest IQR (**USD 10**); Very Good's IQR is **USD 12**, and Excellent's **USD 11.50**. The distributions overlap. The ordered ratings are associated with different observed price centers, but the data do not isolate causal effects or predict an individual's price change.

## 6. Limitations and complementary measures

```{r}
illustrations <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/measure_limitations_examples.csv"))
dollars <- subset(illustrations, example == "extreme_value")$value
stopifnot(nrow(illustrations) == 32, sum(dollars) == 113, median(dollars) == 3)
kable(data.frame(Mean_USD = mean(dollars), Median_USD = median(dollars)), digits = 2)
sets <- subset(illustrations, example == "same_mean")
comparisons <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(sets$value, sets$series), function(v)
  data.frame(Mean = mean(v), Range = diff(range(v)))))
stopifnot(all(comparisons$Mean == 200), all(comparisons$Range == c(200,0,600,1200,4500)))
kable(comparisons)
ab <- subset(illustrations, example == "same_range")
ab_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ab$value, ab$series), function(v)
  data.frame(Mean = mean(v), Range = diff(range(v)),
             Mean_absolute_deviation = mean(abs(v-mean(v))), Sample_SD = sd(v))))
stopifnot(all(ab_summary$Mean == 5), all(ab_summary$Range == 10),
          all(ab_summary$Mean_absolute_deviation == c(2,4)),
          abs(ab_summary$Sample_SD[1]-sqrt(12.5)) < 1e-10, ab_summary$Sample_SD[2] == 5)
kable(ab_summary, digits = 2)
```

The dollar mean is **16.14**, while the median is **3**. Six of seven values lie between 1 and 3. The median better describes the middle, while the mean remains relevant to the total of 113. Preserve a valid large observation.

S1–S5 share mean **200** but ranges **200, 0, 600, 1200, 4500**. Center alone conceals their variation. A and B share mean **5** and range **10**, while mean absolute deviations are **2 and 4** and sample SDs are **3.54 and 5**. B places more observations at the endpoints.

SD uses all observations and responds to internal spread, but squared deviations also emphasize extremes. Median and IQR describe the central portion with less sensitivity to tail magnitudes. A plot reveals gaps, clusters, shape, and tail detail that these summaries omit. No single measure answers every descriptive question. R's `mad()` is not the mean absolute deviation used here.

## Teaching notes

- Use explicit type-6 quartiles and the same fences in the table and chart. A software default that happens to match Audit is not a universal match.
- Emphasize units: variance in days² or USD²; SD and IQR in days or USD; CV as a percentage; z-score dimensionless.
- Keep original data, hypothetical changes, and checked textbook outputs distinct. These are original course calculations from checked book data.
- Weighted/geometric means and detailed shape rules can be developed where their business questions require them. They are not implicitly claimed covered by this lesson.
